title: 1970 AHSME Problem 32
statement: \(A\) and \(B\) travel around a circular track at uniform speeds in opposite directions, starting from diametrically opposite points. If they start at the same time, meet first after \(B\) has travelled \(100\) yards, and meet a second time \(60\) yards before \(A\) completes one lap, then the circumference of the track in yards is:

solutions.text:
Let the circumference be \(2C.\) At the first meeting, \(B\) has traveled \(100\) yards and \(A\) has traveled \(C-100,\) so their speed ratio is \[ \frac{v_A}{v_B}=\frac{C-100}{100}. \] At the second meeting, \(A\) is \(60\) yards short of one lap, so it has traveled \(2C-60.\) By then their combined distance is \(3C,\) so \(B\) has traveled \(C+60.\) Hence \[ \frac{C-100}{100}=\frac{2C-60}{C+60}. \] Cross-multiplying gives \(C=240,\) so the circumference is \(2C=480\) yards.

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let the circumference be \(2C\) and compare the two runners’ traveled-distance ratios at each meeting
At the first meeting their distances are \(C-100\) and \(100\); at the second they are \(2C-60\) and \(C+60\)
